newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw sees 1997 as profitable year.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw sees 1997 as profitable year.

text.p: Transportation and waste firm Laidlaw Inc will post profitable growth in 1997, aided by a proposed merger with American Medical Response, Inc, said chief executive James Bullock on Monday.
Bullock called the giant's first quarter earnings, US$0.22 a share versus year-earlier US$0.18, "a fine start for fiscal 1997."
Laidlaw announced the US$1.12 billion merger on January 6, along with a reverse takeover of Delaware-based Rollins Environmental Services Inc for a total of over US$2 billion.

Bullock said in a statement: "The ongoing strength of our transportation businesses along with our previously announced, proposed merger with American Medical Response, Inc. -- the largest healthcare transportation company in the United States -- and the plan to reshape our Environmental Services unit into a publicly traded entity through a merger with Rollins Environmental Services, Inc., should all contribute to another year of profitable growth."
Chief financial officer Les Haworth, told Reuters in a phone interview that "we expect to expand both the top line and the bottom line" but refused to speculate by how much.
Laidlaw will not see a substantial benefit from the mergers until 1997's third quarter for American Medical Response and the fourth quarter for Rollins, Haworth said.
